title: Do ATS Scores Follow You From Job to Job?
description:
Do ATS scores really follow you from company to company?

A viral claim says that once you get a low ATS score, it follows you to every job you apply for and hurts your chances of getting hired. In this video, I break down what the Stanford study actually found, what it didn't find, and what job seekers should focus on instead.

The truth is that getting interviews isn't about beating a secret ATS score. It's about communicating your value clearly, showing employers how you solve problems, and making it easy for recruiters and hiring managers to understand why you're worth interviewing.

If you're struggling to get interviews, wondering how ATS systems work, trying to improve your resume, or navigating today's competitive job market, you're in the right place.

transcript: Jobseekers are being lied to again. The Stanford study that just went viral did not prove that your ATS score follows you from company to company. You've probably seen people claiming that once you get assigned a low ATS score, you're basically doomed and it's going to follow you no matter where you apply. That's simply not what the study found. The researchers weren't even studying resumes. They were studying game-based assessments that applicants completed during the hiring process, which in my opinion is also problematic, but it's a very different story from the universal ATS score. So, why is everyone saying that's what the study found? It's because fear sells. A secret score ruining your job search is much more clickable than the truth. But, here's the real takeaway. The job market is incredibly competitive right now, and instead of worrying about a fake score, focus on communicating your value clearly and quickly, and making it easy for recruiters to understand why you are aligned with their position and how you can solve their problems. That's what gets interviews, and not viral myths. Follow my career advice that's based on reality, not fear tactics at Krushna Careers.
